Subject: Weekly sales/finance/infra pipeline bridgecall — capacity asks & prioritization

Hi all,

Following up to start a standing weekly bridgecall to align on Dedicated capacity sizing tied to pipeline forecasts. We have a handful of near-term asks from Orion (see attached) and want to make sure infra, finance and sales prioritize consistently as other deals mature.

Proposed weekly slot: Tuesdays 3:30–4:00pm PT (15 min agenda + 15 min buffer) — can tweak if this conflicts.

Agenda for first call (15 min):
- Quick pipeline snapshot: Orion ask + 2 other near-close deals (Ben/Karthik) — 5 min
- Infra constraints & alternative strategies (Logan) — 5 min
- Finance impacts & billing cadence (Laura) — 3 min
- Action items & next steps (Marissa) — 2 min

Attachments: orion_capacity_asks_q3.xlsx (tabbed w/preferred reserve, burst, and fallback model variants), q3_capacity_heatmap_v2.pdf (current pool saturation forecast).

Immediate asks before the call:
1) Ben/Karthik — please mark which deals are highest priority if we only have one burst tranche in early Aug.
2) Logan — highlight any hard constraints (node delivery windows, infra maintenance blackout) and recommended mitigations.
3) Laura — high-level Opex/CapEx flags if we commit to the two-week reserved window in July.

Sophie — thanks for coordinating on your end. If procurement can confirm earliest PO window (approx date) that would help us narrow the slot.

Call invite will follow once everyone confirms the recurring time.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Subject: Re: Weekly sales/finance/infra pipeline bridgecall — capacity asks & prioritization

Marissa — thanks for setting this up. Quick prelim notes from infra before the call:

- Hardware delivery windows: our next modest node replenishment arrives 7/20; large tranche not until mid-September. That means hard limit on adding guaranteed Reserved capacity for early Aug unless we re-balance existing pools.
- Maintenance blackout: Aug 5–9 (data center planned networking work). Avoid scheduled rollout windows during that week.
- Burst strategy: we can usually accommodate short-lived burst by allowing cross-pool spill with a soft-SLO for latency (adds ~150–250ms p99 tails for seq len 1024).
- Alternative: recommend a hybrid for Orion — reserve a small guaranteed pool + a burst credit plan. This reduces initial committed spend but keeps headroom.

I'll bring a short heatmap (live) showing pool occupancy and which reservations we could flex. Also attaching a compact CSV with pool IDs and available vGPU-equivalents.

Logistics ask: if sales can indicate definitive start window (±2 weeks) we can run a pre-commit simulation to show expected p50/p95 latencies under their traffic profile.

— Logan

Folks — quick finance read:

- If we move to a hybrid (small reserved + burst credits) for Orion, the expected revenue recognition will be split: 30% upfront on reservation activation, remainder as usage — better for cashflow than pure burst.
- CapEx hit for adding nodes ahead of schedule is material; need sign-off for any capacity that requires procurement acceleration. If sales can put a tentative commit (signed PO or LOI) that materially changes the ask, we can accelerate procurement approvals but will need projected ARR and expected runrate.
- Short ask for the first call: Ben/Karthik, please add an "expected % of traffic in first 90 days" column to the spreadsheet. Finance uses that for our ROI sensitivity.

I will be on the call and can run a quick cost delta slide (3 bullets).
